title: Kodaira vanishing over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Y$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral $F$-scheme of pure dimension $n\ge0$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Define $\omega_Y=\bigwedge^n\Omega^1_{Y/F}$. The sheaf $\Omega^1_{Y/F}$ is obtained by gluing the modules of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{A/F}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] on affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$. For a locally free module $E$, $\bigwedge^n E$ is its alternating exterior power (the quotient of $E^{\otimes n}$ by the alternating multilinearity relations), with $\bigwedge^0 E=\mathcal O_Y$. Let $A$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module, def-sc-invertible-module]. Then $$H^i(Y,\omega_Y\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}A)=0\qquad(i>0),$$ where $H^i=R^i\Gamma$ is Zariski module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology] and tensor product is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

proof.text: Projectivity gives properness. Apply the proper-field coherence lemma with the invertible module $\mathcal O_Y$: $Y$ is Noetherian and $\mathcal O_Y$ is coherent. Smoothness gives finite locally free $\Omega^1_{Y/F}$. On a trivializing open with basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, the wedges $e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_n}$ for $i_1<\cdots<i_n$ form a finite basis of $\omega_Y$ (the single empty wedge for $n=0$). Thus locally $\omega_Y$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_Y$. Finite sums of coherent modules are coherent by the cited closure lemma; coherence is local directly from its definition. Consequently $\omega_Y$ is coherent. This argument does not assume a rank formula for the differential sheaf.

The base ring $F$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $F$. Serre vanishing, with coefficient $\mathcal F=\omega_Y$ and ample invertible module $A$, gives $a$ such that $H^i(Y,\omega_Y\otimes A^{\otimes t})=0$ for every $i>0$ and $t\geq a$. Since $Y$ is proper over $F$ (step 1) and, by the definition of ampleness, every point of $Y$ lies in an affine open $Y_\sigma$ for some $\sigma\in\Gamma(Y,A^{\otimes k})$, $k\geq1$, the affine-loci criterion shows that $A$ is ample in the sense used by the sections lemma (some positive power has a complete linear system giving a closed immersion). Apply the sections lemma with closed subscheme $Z=\varnothing$: for all sufficiently large $m$, $V_m=\Gamma(Y,A^{\otimes m})$ generates $A^{\otimes m}$ and gives an immersion into $\mathbf P(V_m)$. Choose such an $m\geq2$ with $m+1\geq a$. The module $A^{\otimes m}$ is invertible, hence coherent by the proper-field coherence lemma. Projective coherent finiteness makes $V_m$ finite-dimensional over $F$. Since $Y$ is nonempty and this space generates a line bundle, $r=\dim_F V_m\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 02O1 (lemma-kill-by-twisting); Varieties Tag 0FD5 (lemma-generate-over-complement). Popa, proof of Theorem 1.6.1, printed pp.27--28, simultaneous choice of the power.

proof.text: Apply Bertini to the generating space $V_m$, the invertible module $A^{\otimes m}$ and the immersion from step 2. Its conclusion gives a nonempty open $U\subset\mathbf A^r_F$ parametrizing sections with smooth zero scheme. Intersect with $\mathbf A^r_F\setminus\{0\}$; it remains nonempty since $r\geq1$ and affine space is integral. This open contains a principal open $D(f)$ with $f$ a nonzero polynomial. A nonzero polynomial over the infinite field $F$ is nonzero at some tuple in $F^r$: induct on $r$, first choosing values where a nonzero coefficient does not vanish, and then avoiding the finitely many roots in the last variable. Such a tuple yields $0\ne s\in\Gamma(Y,A^{\otimes m})$ and a smooth zero scheme $D=Z(s)$. Empty $D$ is permitted, in particular when $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0FD6 (lemma-bertini), with the elementary rational-coefficient choice written out; Popa, proof of Theorem 1.6.1, printed pp.27--28.

proof.text: Apply the smooth-divisor injectivity theorem with $L=A$, the integer $m\geq2$ and the section $s$ of step 3. All hypotheses hold over the given algebraically closed characteristic-zero field; no embedding of $F$ in $\mathbf C$ is assumed. It gives an injection $H^i(Y,\omega_Y\otimes A)\longrightarrow H^i(Y,\omega_Y\otimes A^{\otimes(m+1)})$ for every $i\geq0$.

proof.text: For $i>0$ the target of the injection in step 4 is zero by step 2 because $m+1\geq a$. Every element of its source has the same image as zero, so injectivity forces it to be zero. Hence $H^i(Y,\omega_Y\otimes A)=0$ for every $i>0$, including in dimension zero.
